standard_prerequisites.name: Situation ABC
standard_prerequisites.statement: The author's standing situation: a differential graded category with admissible monomorphisms, admissible short exact sequences and the associated graded additive category.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the setting of the statement and of axiom (A) used at source line 4655 (source line 4578).

standard_prerequisites.name: Distinguished triangles from admissible short exact sequences
standard_prerequisites.statement: Every admissible short exact sequence extends to a distinguished triangle, with the connecting map defined as pi d(s) for chosen splittings, and the resulting triangles satisfy the triangle identities (the author's lemma-get-triangle, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It produces the three triangles and supplies every computational identity used in the proof (source lines 4587-4615, 4636-4644, 4674-4675).

standard_prerequisites.name: Biproduct and kernel in an additive category
standard_prerequisites.statement: In an additive category, the kernel of the projection of a biproduct onto its first factor can be computed as the complementary summand (Homology, Lemma homology-lemma-additive-cat-biproduct-kernel, declared as a tagged source pointer).
standard_prerequisites.use: It gives q_2 = q_1 direct sum q_3 in the underlying graded category (source lines 4657-4666).

standard_prerequisites.name: The octahedral axiom TR4
standard_prerequisites.statement: The statement of TR4 for two composable morphisms in a triangulated category.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what the constructed triangles are asserted to satisfy (source line 4582).

core_obligations: Construct the three triangles and their connecting maps: extend the admissible short exact sequences for alpha, beta alpha and beta to distinguished triangles and define delta_i = pi_i d(s_i) (source lines 4585-4615).

Build the octahedron: fill the solid commutative diagram with the two dashed maps p_2 beta s_1 and p_3 s_2 and verify that both are morphisms of complexes using the identities of the triangle lemma (source lines 4616-4644).

Show admissible exactness of the middle sequence: prove that q_1 -> q_2 -> q_3 is an admissible short exact sequence, i.e. that the underlying graded object q_2 is q_1 direct sum q_3 with the dashed maps as coprojection and projection (source lines 4644-4668).
Identify the connecting morphism: check that the connecting map delta of that sequence equals p_1 delta_3, so that the constructed triangles satisfy TR4 (source lines 4670-4687).

proof_roadmap.step: Extend the three admissible short exact sequences to distinguished triangles and define the connecting maps delta_i.
Fill the octahedral diagram with the two dashed maps and check they are morphisms of complexes.
Prove q_1 to q_2 to q_3 is admissible by identifying q_2 with q_1 direct sum q_3 via the biproduct-kernel lemma.
Compute the connecting map of the new sequence and identify it with p_1 delta_3 to conclude TR4.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-dgc-analogue-tr4 at source lines 4576-4583: in the author's Situation ABC, two composable admissible monomorphisms x -> y -> z can be completed to distinguished triangles for which the octahedral axiom TR4 holds. The proof at source lines 4585-4688 is a hundred-line explicit construction: three admissible short exact sequences are extended to triangles, the octahedral diagram is filled with two dashed maps built from the chosen splittings, those maps are checked to be morphisms of complexes using the computational identities of the author's triangle lemma, the middle object q_2 is identified with q_1 direct sum q_3 in the underlying graded category via a biproduct-kernel lemma of the Homology chapter, and finally the connecting morphism of the new triangle is identified with p_1 delta_3 by an explicit four-term computation. Nothing here is conceptual in the way TR4 is for the derived category; the substance is the bookkeeping of splittings and signs, which is why the card is rated higher than the chapter's short lemmas.
